# Workflow Conventions

## Three workflow files split by triggering event

Verification certifies on PRs; delivery runs on the landing push. `integrate.yml` (triggers `pull_request: [dev]` + `workflow_dispatch`; concurrency `group: integrate-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true` — a superseded PR run cancels whole) runs the entire verify DAG. `release.yml` (triggers `push: [main, dev]`; concurrency `group: release-${{ github.ref }}` with NO cancel — the queue is the policy: overlapping `main` releases wait their turn so `release` can never die mid-release, and queued dev runs guarantee every merge to `dev` gets its prerelease set 1:1) runs the delivery jobs gated by branch: `prerelease` on `dev`, `release` on `main`. `merge-gate.yml` is the third file — the bors-model lander, dual-triggered on the `ready-to-merge` label event (consent wake) and Integrate's green completion (readiness wake, via `workflow_run` — the one sanctioned carve-out of the org-wide delivery-bridge ban: merge-gate's completion wake only; the verb re-asserts the label because the workflow_run payload carries no labels and no PR number), per-PR concurrency group with NO cancel (serialization gives every wake a complete execution; the verb is idempotent); release-devkit's `AGENTS.md` owns the full contract. No other `workflow_run` use (a push run re-verifying what a PR already certified would be double-running) and no `pull_request: [main]` (the standing release PR's head is the dev tip that already ran identical CI; it reports zero checks, and `main` branch protection must require none). The delivery jobs stand alone — a standing release-PR tracking a red `dev` branch is the accurate state.

The verify DAG (`lint-workflows`, `validate-release-plan`, and `mirror-images` are the parallel roots; `needs` is transitive — ancestors are never re-listed):

```
lint-workflows ─┐
mirror-images ──┴→ preflight ─┐
validate-release-plan ─────────┼→ get-docker-matrix → build-docker → publish-compose
                               └→ get-unity-matrix → preflight-unity
```

`mirror-images` stays a root rather than a child because the repo-specific preflight builds the postgres wrapper image, whose `FROM` is a mirror-prefixed base from `workloads/images.lock`, so the mirror namespace must be populated before `preflight` pulls from it — and because `preflight` needs `mirror-images` (plus `lint-workflows`, so contract breaks kill the battery early), a cycle is forbidden, making `mirror-images` a parallel root rather than a child. Matrix getters `needs: [preflight, validate-release-plan]`: the battery chain and the plan root fail fast in their own lanes.

## Shared devkit operations: wrapper-installed release-devkit, inline `uv run` for the rest

Shared devkit operations split by consumption model. release-devkit cannot be a project dependency (it sits inside every consumer's own dependency graph), so it is installed onto the runner by `.github/actions/setup-release-devkit` — a one-step composite that clones the devkit at a pinned SHA into `$RUNNER_TEMP/release-devkit`, the only place the SHA appears. Each verb-owning job prepares checkout → `setup-uv` → wrapper → verb, and the verbs are plain run steps (`uv run --project "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-devkit" --locked --no-dev <verb>`) — see release-devkit's `AGENTS.md` for the consumption shape. The `lint-workflows` job (checkout, restore setup-uv, wrapper, the `lint-workflows` run step) never carries tokens; the `preflight` job (checkout, the repo's one cache-writing setup-uv, then the repo battery) needs `[lint-workflows, mirror-images]`; the `validate-release-plan` job (checkout-with-tags, restore setup-uv, wrapper, the `validate-release-plan` run step) is the plan-time gate. `preflight`'s setup-uv is the single cache writer in the file; every other job restores (`save-cache: "false"`). unity-devkit is a PyPI dev-group dependency like the others, so its verbs run inline as `uv run` (version-sourced by `uv.lock`): `get-unity-matrix` runs `uv run compile-check-unity-matrix` (emitting the include matrix plus the license tag), and each `preflight-unity` leg runs `uv run compile-check-unity` inside its `matrix.editor-image` `unityci/editor` container on self-hosted `unity` runners — license restore-or-activate and the UPM cache are verb-internal. Every other devkit (`python-devkit`, `docker-devkit`, `openapi-client-codegen`) is a PyPI dependency the same way: `mirror-images` runs `uv run mirror`; the `preflight` job runs `uv run --no-sync preflight-python` (the python battery) then `uv run --no-sync preflight` (repo-specific checks) then `uv run --no-sync generate-clients --check` (openapi staleness gate); `get-docker-matrix` runs `uv run docker-build-matrix` (one entry per variant, targets grouped by dependency closure — dependents with the base their `additional_contexts: target:` references pull in); `build-docker` and `publish-compose` run repo-local scripts (`build-docker --variant ${{ matrix.variant }} --targets ${{ matrix.targets }}` per leg, QEMU kept). Every `uv run` in the battery auto-syncs internally (`--no-sync` on the outer steps because the battery's first step is the full sync; everything after re-syncs its own context anyway).

## PyPI matrix eliminated — trusted publishing, no environments

Both PyPI packages (`placeframe-common`, `placeframe-core-python`) publish from the single `release` job (and the single `prerelease` job) — no per-package matrix. No job carries an `environment:` key: the org's `release` environments were vestigial and are scrubbed fleet-wide. PyPI's OIDC trusted-publishing rows are keyed `(owner, repo, workflow_filename)` — operator-audited: every placeframe publisher row is environment-less, and warehouse only enforces an environment when a row specifies one, so the environment-less jobs match the configured publishers exactly (the earlier `(owner, repo, workflow_filename, environment)` keying claim was wrong, as was the "one `release` environment shared by both channels" framing). npm trusted publishers are bound to `release.yml` (one publisher per package, single workflow filename). nuget joins them the same way: the nuget.org trusted-publishing policy is owner/repo `outernet-foundation/placeframe` + workflow file `release.yml` + blank environment — matching the environment-less jobs — so `release.yml` must never be renamed (already npm law, now nuget law too). Both delivery jobs mint the short-lived nuget key with the official `NuGet/login@v1` step (`id: nuget-login`, `user` from the `NUGET_USER` org secret — the nuget.org profile name that owns `PlaceframeApiClient`, a routing parameter, not a credential) between the devkit wrapper and the verb, and the verb env reads `NUGET_API_KEY: ${{ steps.nuget-login.outputs.NUGET_API_KEY }}`; no nuget credential lives in the secret store. The human gate for delivery is the `dev` → `main` release PR. `release` has no artifact stapling — placeframe declares no app builds shelves, so its releases carry the release notes only; `create-release` runs inside the command whenever something published.

All workflow logic lives in Python scripts (release-devkit commands as run steps from the wrapper-installed clone, repo-local scripts via `uv run`) — no inline shell conditionals or loops.
